reviewer_role: Senior AppSec engineer reviewing junior study material

issues.title: mechanism.trust-boundary-confusion's authority_transition wording is SSRF-shaped
issues.description: The mechanism's authority_transition field states the privileged component 'executes the operation using its own ambient authority (network position, local socket, or IAM role)', which describes a server performing an action against a third party on the attacker's behalf. Host header attacks do not fit this: the server does not perform a privileged operation against an external target. It generates or caches OUTPUT that a separate trusting party later acts on.
issues.recommendation: Do not silently reinterpret. Either broaden the mechanism's authority_transition language, or split into a sibling mechanism. Escalate to Pass 3 arbitration.

self_review_caveat: Pass 1 draft and Pass 2 review were produced in the same authoring session without a distinct reviewer identity; confirmation bias on the drafter's own causal claims — particularly ISSUE-01's mechanism-scope judgment — has not been independently checked. This is the same limitation already documented for topic.ssrf and remains an open process gap, not one resolved by this topic.
